summary.summary: South Kesteven's debt is all housing (HRA) borrowing and edged down to £76.548m at an average 2.57%, against a capital financing requirement of £102.722m — so £26.174m of the borrowing need is covered by the council's own cash rather than loans. The story is on the cash side: investments fell from £62.767m to £43.141m because the capital programme was paid for wholly from reserves, and the council itself says cashflow management is becoming more challenging as reserve levels continue to decrease. Investment income of £2.718m came in £0.030m under budget after HRA reserves were drawn to meet in-year spending pressures. Internal audit gave the treasury function a substantial assurance opinion, and there were no liquidity difficulties in the year.

signals.headline: Investments fell £19.6m in 2025/26 (£62.767m to £43.141m) as capital spend was funded wholly from reserves; council flags cashflow management getting harder as reserves keep decreasing
signals.why: The internal cash that currently substitutes for £26.174m of borrowing is shrinking, bringing forward the point where external borrowing is needed.

news_drafts.headline: South Kesteven's borrowing stands at £74.9m, all from the PWLB, at an average rate of 2.52%
news_drafts.lead:
South Kesteven District Council's borrowing stood at £74.937m on 30 September 2026, all of it from the Public Works Loan Board (PWLB), the government's lending arm for councils. The Governance and Audit Committee's quarter 2 treasury update on 5 November reports an average interest rate of 2.52% on the debt portfolio and says no additional borrowing was required in the second quarter of 2026/27.

The paper's maturity table shows £3.222m due for repayment within one year and £41.109m due between five and ten years. All of the debt is classed under the housing revenue account, the ring-fenced account for the council's own housing stock, which is paid for by rents.

The paper also gives a figure for debt at 31 March of £66.881m, against £74.937m at 30 September. It does not reconcile the two in the text. Existing debt at 1 April is given as £70.103m. The paper says regular reviews are carried out to compare the cost of repaying loans early with letting them run to maturity and with taking new borrowing.

news_drafts.headline: South Kesteven's council tax billing error forces cashflow recalculation
news_drafts.lead: South Kesteven District Council's revenue team processed an August council tax direct debit five days early in July, calling in £6.5m from 36,079 customers by mistake. The error resulted from a single officer failing to change the system default processing date, with no independent check before the file was uploaded and became irreversible. The council has introduced a new control requiring two revenue team leaders and the head of service to verify the date same-day, with all checks completed before submission. Governance and Audit Committee heard that 1,594 customers—4.4 per cent of those affected—chose to spread their August instalment over the remainder of the financial year rather than pay by other means, which the council acknowledges could affect collection rates. The early income forced a recalculation of the council's cashflow projections for the rest of the year.

news_drafts.headline: South Kesteven forecasts budget deficits from 2027/28 as government funding falls
news_drafts.lead: South Kesteven District Council faces structural deficits from 2027/28 onwards as government funding reduces over a three-year settlement period, according to papers reviewed by the Finance and Economic Overview and Scrutiny Committee. While a one-off grant mitigates funding losses in 2026/27, the council has no guarantee of additional support in future years, the papers state. The deficit forecast will require the council to cut spending to balance its budget. Separately, the council's housing account faces pressure from an unsustainable capital programme that will significantly reduce reserves over three years, forcing a fundamental review of investment priorities using stock condition data. The building control partnership that South Kesteven runs with two other councils showed improved financial performance, with fee income £21,000 above budget, though Rushcliffe Borough Council reported a deficit while the other two partners showed surpluses.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A – Corporate Plan 2024-27 KPI Report: Governance & Audit Committee Mid-Year (Q2) 2026/27
findings.headline: Housing Stage 1 complaints 77.58% resolved on time and Stage 2 complaints 91.6%, with 0 Ombudsman determinations against the council in Q2 2026/27.
findings.detail: The paper reports 60 Stage 1 and 14 Stage 2 housing complaints in Q2. It records 23 ongoing Ombudsman cases and 7 new cases during the quarter, with no determinations against the council.
findings.matters: Ombudsman determinations and open case volume are a measure of housing service risk that a lender or finance director would weigh alongside housing revenue exposure.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A – Corporate Plan 2024-27 KPI Report: Governance & Audit Committee Mid-Year (Q2) 2026/27
findings.headline: 72.27% of councillors have completed all four mandatory training topics at Q2 2026/27, against a 100% target.
findings.detail: The paper gives completion by topic: Code of Conduct 72.73% (40 of 55), EDI 65.45% (36 of 55), PREVENT 76.36% (42 of 55) and Safeguarding 74.54% (41 of 55). Figures are adjusted for one vacancy in Grantham St Wulfram's ward.
findings.matters: Member training completion underpins the governance assurance the audit committee relies on, and the topic-level figures show where completion lags.

findings.quote: As of the end of Q2 2026/27, 72.27% of members have completed all four mandatory topics.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A – Corporate Plan 2024-27 KPI Report: Governance & Audit Committee Mid-Year (Q2) 2026/27
findings.headline: Councillor Development Charter programme on hold since April 2025, with the project under review by the new Monitoring Officer and Cabinet member.
findings.detail: The paper says a new Monitoring Officer was appointed in January 2026, and the project is now being reviewed by that officer and the Cabinet member. The KPI remains Below Target at Q2 2026/27.
findings.matters: A stalled accreditation programme with a changed post holder is a governance point that peer councils and external reviewers may compare against their own progress.
findings.figures: On hold since April 2025; new Monitoring Officer appointed January 2026
findings.quote: The programme has been on hold since April 2025.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A – Corporate Plan 2024-27 KPI Report: Governance & Audit Committee Mid-Year (Q2) 2026/27
findings.headline: 25% of 12 Subject Access Requests answered within the 90% target timescale in Q2 2026/27, with 75% overdue.
findings.detail: The paper links the shortfall to capacity and staff turnover in the team, while SAR complexity has increased. Recruitment is under way for an interim Data Protection Officer solution to add capacity.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council will recognise the pattern of a small data protection team losing capacity, and a council with overdue SARs carries regulatory exposure.
findings.figures: 12 SARs received; 25% closed on time; 75% overdue; 90% target
findings.quote: Twelve SARs were received in Q2. 25% were responded to within the defined target time.
